scope: Frozen development rubric only; anonymous P/Q reports; no held-out grading.
interpretation_notes: Evidence paths are relative to the frozen snapshot; candidate line references point to the separate input reports. Listed source anchors support the scored relationship, not every detail in the report.
Whole-report causal explanations count across task sections where explicitly connected; repeating scheduler lifecycle prose is not required.
Additional filenames, report length, process self-labels and non-rubric details receive no extra credit. Unneeded taskContext implementation claims were not independently inspected or rewarded.

Plain path versus structural-path routing was checked against queryCli.ts:70-100. Q explicitly uses structural-path; P's generic statement that the CLI also consumes snapshots does not claim that every CLI command uses the structural store.
No test execution or packaged-VSIX proof is credited. Both reports frame test coverage and proposals appropriately.

rubric_flaws.description: The item bundles non-abortion and non-awaiting in one score. Q explicitly covers only the former, so frozen partial-credit rules produce 0.5. Treating its cited implementation or 'continues' wording as sufficient implicit coverage is the main consequential judgment to audit.
The frozen item specifically requires MCP consumers in addition to GraphView. Q's correct CLI-to-the-same-store trace is useful but does not replace that named MCP link under the frozen criterion.

audit_notes.assessment: Correct non-abortion, not a false claim; missing explicit disposal non-await contract.

audit_notes.quote: Query CLI `context`, `impact`, `structural-path` and `structure` also read the existing structural snapshot; diff reads the previous snapshot.
audit_notes.assessment: Correct routing; partial credit is for omitted MCP consumers, not a routing error.
Read as suffix shorthand for the previous structural snapshot, not a materially false claim that the actual basename is literally .previous.json.
Recovery and reader-cache tests do not replace the absent source-content-hash freshness regression.
